content.text:
No. Nobody has been told about it, by me or by the pipeline.

- The original 11-04 nightly crashed in the review step before it reached the alerting code. That run never alerted anyone.
- My rerun had `no_notify = true`, so it recorded the finding but queued no alerts. There was no `spool/outgoing/` directory afterward, so the relay had nothing to deliver.
- I didn't send any messages myself, per your rule.

The finding exists only in local files, `data/findings/2026-11-04.jsonl` and `out/review-2026-11-04.json`. It never reached `/srv/acme/review-findings` either, because that path was the one that failed.

Under normal operation, a severity-3 finding like this one ("agent wrote outside its workspace: `/home/runner/shared/eval-cache/index.json`") would have pinged `security-oncall@acme.dev` and `agent-safety@acme.dev` and paged `sec-pager@acme.dev`. I'd tell the security on-call yourself. Their sign-off was for the rerun, and they may not know this particular finding came out of it. If you want the pipeline to send the normal alerts instead, I can rerun the review with alerts on, but only if you tell me to, since that would mean sending messages.
